title: QBR - EmberCore quarterly business review
summary: Quarterly business review covering usage trends, cost drivers, two recent reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Customer is leaning toward reserved capacity for predictable latency but wants detailed cost modelling and a short benchmark on their peak workload. Security and audit logs are gating for Private/VPC evaluation.
topics: recent latency incidents and root cause
security controls: SOC2, SSO, KMS and audit logs
next steps: pricing, benchmark, security docs
action_items: Samira Patel: Send detailed reserved capacity pricing + example TCO spreadsheet; due 2026-09-16
Alex Chen: Schedule a 2-hour technical benchmark with EmberCore infra team and provide runbook; due 2026-09-18
Diego Marquez: Share SOC2 artifacts and network architecture checklist for Private deployment; due 2026-09-14
Maya Thompson: Provide representative prompt set and peak QPS window for benchmark; due 2026-09-12
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and TCO workbook
Follow-up QBR in 6 weeks to review pilot results
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~60m | Attendees: Samira P (Redwood AE), Alex C (Redwood SE), Diego M (Redwood CSM) -- Maya T (EmberCore, Head of ML Ops), Ethan R (Platform), Priya N (CTO)

00:00:03 Samira (Redwood AE): Thanks everyone for joining, this is the EmberCore QBR — quick agenda, usage and cost, reliability incidents, roadmap alignment, and next steps. if we hit something we can always do a follow-up deep dive.
00:00:18 Maya (EmberCore): Yep sounds good. thanks Samira. I just wanted to flag up front that costs have increased last quarter because of a new recommender model we pushed.
00:00:26 Samira: Understood, we'll pull the detailed token breakout. Diego, you had the usage dashboard?
00:00:31 Diego (Redwood CSM): Yep, I pulled the dashboard. Ehm, monthly token consumption is up ~42% q/q, embedding calls stable, but generation tokens spiked during the Nov-release test. we saw average latency creep from 180ms to about 260ms on P95 for the 2x models.
00:00:48 Ethan (EmberCore): Right, and that P95 is causing timeouts on some of our synchronous flows. we've been falling back to cached responses but it's not ideal.
00:00:54 Alex (Redwood SE): Quick Q — are you on hosted or dedicated today?
00:00:58 Maya: We're on hosted API with higher concurrency keys for prod, no dedicated yet.
00:01:03 Alex: That explains part of it. For predictable P95 you'd get benefits from dedicated pools and pinning model versions; also batching and KV cache tuning helps for your prefix-heavy load.
00:01:14 Priya (CTO): We're evaluating Dedicated but security wants the VPC/private option as well. can you enumerate the security controls for Private?
00:01:22 Diego: Sure — we support VPC peering, customer-managed KMS/HSM, SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. I can share the SOC2 & architecture playbook after the call.
00:01:31 Priya: Great. audit logs are critical for our compliance team. also encryption at rest and in flight — are there options for customer-owned keys?
00:01:38 Samira: Yes KMS integration is supported for Private; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key via our managed KMS options depending on the contract.
00:01:46 Maya: Back to cost — can you show how batching could reduce our per-token bill? we have a lot of short queries.
00:01:52 Alex: Absolutely. For short prompt distributions batching can reduce GPU overhead; plus we recommend quantized variants for non-sensitive workloads. we'll include modeled savings in the TCO workbook.
00:02:01 Ethan: A quick question on model variants — if we move to a quantized variant do we see regression on quality? we've been tracking relevance metrics and don't want regression.
00:02:09 Alex: There's tradeoffs — 4-bit quant can be fine for many tasks but ROGUE edge cases happen. we usually run evals on your prompt set and surface delta in the eval dashboard before recommending rollout.
00:02:20 Maya: Would you run that eval as part of the benchmark?
00:02:22 Alex: Yes we'll run both latency/throughput benchmarks and a quality eval on the provided prompt set.
00:02:27 Samira: Quick recap of incidents — Maya you mentioned two incidents last month? can you walk through briefly?
00:02:33 Maya: Sure. On Aug 14th we had a 40m window where requests spiked because of an integration test; the autoscaler delayed adding capacity due to our long-tail concurrency profile, so P95 spiked and some requests timed out. second was a shorter 12m KV cache miss storm during a deployment, cache re-population caused more backend hits.
00:02:53 Alex: That cache re-pop storm is a known pattern; we can suggest warmup strategies, and our autoscaler policy can be tuned for your QPS spikes.
00:02:59 Ethan: Also slightly worried about cross-region failover; we saw routing fallback add ~150ms.
00:03:04 Diego: We have smart routing policies — you can prefer region A and failover to region B, and we can set latency thresholds. we'll share configuration examples.
00:03:11 Priya: For the dedicated option, what are SLA numbers?
00:03:13 Samira: Dedicated has a latency and uptime SLA; I'll send the SLA doc. generally uptime SLA is 99.95 and we target P95 latency buckets depending on committed throughput.
00:03:23 Maya: Pricing ask — can you provide committed monthly pricing + burst costs for peak?
00:03:28 Samira: We'll include reserved capacity tiers in the pricing workbook with burst and overage rules.
00:03:33 Maya: Cool. also can you show an example of cost with quantization + batching for our 200 QPS peak window?
00:03:40 Alex: We'll model that; bring your peak profile and prompt set, and we'll run a benchmark so the numbers are real.
00:03:46 Samira: let's talk timeline — EmberCore wants to make a decision in the next 4 weeks?
00:03:50 Priya: Yes, preferably 3-4 weeks. security review is the gating item for Private.
00:03:55 Diego: We'll prioritize sending SOC2 artifacts and the network checklist tomorrow.
00:03:59 Maya: One more question — do you support audit log retention beyond 12 months? compliance may require longer.
00:04:04 Diego: We have add-on packages for extended log retention; we'll include the options and pricing.
00:04:09 Ethan: Is there any integration with our SIEM? we use Splunk.
00:04:12 Diego: Yes Splunk/Datadog integrations are supported via push or syslog.
00:04:16 Maya: okay thanks.
00:04:18 [15:05] Samira: We'll open the screen to show the usage graph — (screen share noise) so here is your monthly tokens, spikes on Aug 14th visible.
00:04:32 Ethan: yep that's the test spike.
00:04:35 Samira: For recommendations — 1) reserved capacity for predictable latency, 2) tune autoscaler policy and warmup for KV cache, 3) run quantization evals on your prompt set, 4) plan a 2-hour benchmark to validate peak performance.
00:04:52 Priya: Sounds reasonable. For the benchmark what infra access do you need?
00:04:56 Alex: We'll need an ephemeral key, sample prompt set, and a small test node in your VPC if you want private-to-private testing; otherwise we can run benchmarks from our dedicated test harness.
00:05:07 Maya: We'll provide the prompt set and ephemeral key.
00:05:10 Samira: Great. I'm going to summarize action items and next steps at the end and Diego will follow up with SOC2 link.
00:05:18 [crosstalk] Priya: also please put the pricing workbook in a shared drive link.
00:05:23 Samira: Will do.
00:05:25 Alex: Any final questions on reliability or the roadmap?
00:05:28 Maya: On roadmap — do you have timelines for additional model variants that are more cost-efficient?
00:05:33 Samira: We have a model catalog plan, we'll share the upcoming model rollouts; some smaller footprint variants slated next quarter.
00:05:40 Ethan: Are there any known regressions for the models planned? we had one minor semantic shift last release.
00:05:45 Alex: We'll surface model release notes and regression alerts; Redwood Optimize can set regression watches on your eval set.
00:05:52 Maya: ok great. thank you all.
00:05:55 Samira: Thanks everyone. Diego will share SOC2 + network checklist tomorrow; I'll send pricing and TCO workbook by EOD Friday and Alex will schedule the benchmark. follow-up QBR in ~6 weeks post-benchmark.
00:06:10 [meeting end]
notes: Alex to run benchmark and provide runbook
